<meta>continues from previous page: ...which God has destined for their uses and necessity,</meta>

destined, they might penetrate. From these things, conclude that it is necessary that procedures follow my prescription, and by no means yours. Here it is required that you follow me, not I you. And although you may thunder many things against me even yet, my Monarchy shall nevertheless stand, and yours will entirely perish. I do not write so prolixly about Alchemy in vain; rather, I do it with this intention and purpose: that you might know, closely and solidly, what lies hidden within it, and how it ought to be understood. And you should not be offended by the fact that neither gold nor silver emerges from it. But this rather must be attended to: that through it, the <term>arcana</term> <gloss>hidden mysteries/secrets</gloss> may be detected, and the seductions of the <term>seplasiariorum</term> <gloss>perfumers/apothecaries</gloss> betrayed, by which the crude commoners are deceived, while for one florin they serve them what they would not purchase for one coin. Such are their precious secrets.

<margin>Poison even in the best things.</margin>
Who is there who would dare to deny that poison lies hidden and exists even in the best things? All are forced to admit this. If this, therefore, is true, I ask you now: should poison not be separated from the good and the useful? And the good taken, and the evil left behind? Indeed, it must be so. If, therefore, it must be so, I ask you to explain to me: how is it separated in your workshops? For with you, everything remains mixed. But in order to defend your simplicity, if you are convicted of admitting that poison lies there, and you are asked where at last that poison goes: then I do not know what you bring forth regarding "corrections," which allegedly extract and remove the poison,
<margin>The correction of physicians is examined.</margin>
just as they correct Quince with Scammony, or later with <term>Diagridium</term> <gloss>a preparation of scammony</gloss>. But what kind of correction is that? Does the poison not remain afterwards as it was at first? And yet, in the meantime, you boast that you have corrected it, so that the poison no longer harms. But where has it gone?
<margin>Diagridium.</margin>
It remains in the <term>Diagridium</term>. Test this, if you are wise: exceed the measure, and you will see where the poison is. For you will know that not sluggishly. Thus you also correct <term>Turbith</term> <gloss>a purgative root</gloss>, and call it <term>Diaturbith</term>. Such are your corrections, which would befit rustics and should be administered to horses. Make an experiment by exceeding the measure, and increase the dose: you will see if you are not going to feel the poison.
<margin>What a Physician's correction is.</margin>
*To correct is to take the corrected.* Whoever is malicious and has sinned: if he is punished, the correction does not extend further than the will of the one who has been punished lasts. Such are these corrections, too; it is situated with them, not with you. Now, in this case, there is nothing for a Physician to consider further than that the poison be removed. That must be done through separation: as, for example, a serpent is poisonous, and yet it is adopted for food. If you remove the poison from it, you may eat it without any harm. The same must be understood equally concerning all other things, namely, that there is a need for a similar separation. That not yet done, you cannot be secure in your operation: unless perhaps it happens that nature supplies your turns, or the greater beneficence of the heavens favors you. For in your art, there will be no help remaining.

Therefore, since the true foundation—if it is to be called such—is that which removes the poison, [consider] how Alchemy performs this. For this must be done in such a way that, if Mars is in the Sun, Mars is removed, and if Saturn is situated in Venus, it is separated from it. For as many as are the ascendants and impressions in the things of nature, just so many bodies exist in them. But as for those bodies which are contrary, it is necessary that some part of them be entirely removed and taken away, so that in this way all contrariety may be lifted, and the evil may be removed from the good, which is what you seek.
<margin>Fire perfects all things.</margin>
As gold is useless for anything, unless it is first cast into the fire: so much less useful is medicine that does not pass through the fire. For it is necessary that all things pass through fire into another generation, which ought to conduct and assist man. And should this not deservedly be considered the approved foundation of any Physician? For a Physician ought not to apply poisons, but <term>arcana</term> <gloss>secret remedies</gloss>.
<margin>Workshops reprimanded.</margin>
However, all those workshop preparations, however many there are, do not contribute even a letter to this doctrine; rather, they are occupied simply in correcting, just as if a dog has farted in a room, and that stench is subdued either with troches and incense or with juniper wood: does the stench not remain in the room afterwards just as it was before? And although it might not be perceived by smell, is it permitted for anyone to say that the stench has been separated, and no longer remains? No, it is present, but corrected by fumigation. Thus, therefore, the fumigation and the stench enter the nostrils together. Of such a kind also are the corrections of the Pharmacists, who dull an <term>Aleopaticum</term> <gloss>a pain-killing or soothing remedy</gloss> with sugar, so that it may inflict no harm. Thus, sugar and honey are their masteries. In this way, they also correct gentian with theriac. But are these not works of asinine ignorance? They boast and sell themselves as the principal Physicians. Yet who is so stupid that he does not immediately smell that these things are worthless? For what can they boast about their remedies, other than to say, *This Electuary is sweet, made of aromatics and sugar,*

<summary>Paracelsus condemns the common pharmaceutical practice of masking the toxicity of ingredients with additives like sugar or incense, arguing that "correcting" substances without true alchemical separation leaves the poison behind. He maintains that only fire-based alchemical separation can purify medicinal substances to ensure they are safe and effective for human use.</summary>
<keywords>Alchemy, Pharmacy, Medicine, Arcana, Diagridium, Separation, Toxicity, Purification</keywords>

flags.latin: et à bono malum, quod quæris, adimatur.
flags.english: and the evil which you seek may be removed from the good.
flags.problem: The Latin says to remove the evil from the good; the English says to remove the evil which you are seeking.
flags.correct: and the evil may be removed from the good, which is what you seek.
